[2018 summer phd probability — problem 1]

Let $X_1, X_2$ be i.i.d. random variables with a Uniform distribution on $[0,1]$. Further let $T = \max\{X_1, \bar X\}$, where $\bar X$ is the sample mean of $X_1$ and $X_2$.
(a) Find the cumulative distribution function of $T$.
(b) Find $\mathbb{E}[T]$.
(c) Find $\mathbb{E}[X_1 \mid T = t]$ for $0 \le t \le 1$.
(d) Find $\operatorname{Var}[X_1 \mid T = t]$ for $0 \le t \le 1$.

response.text:
Let \(X=X_1\) and \(Y=X_2\). Then \((X,Y)\) is uniform on the unit square, and

\[
T=\max\left\{X,\frac{X+Y}{2}\right\}.
\]

Notice that

\[
X\ge \frac{X+Y}{2}\iff X\ge Y.
\]

Hence, up to a null set,

\[
T=
\begin{cases}
X, & Y\le X,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{X+Y}{2}, & Y>X.
\end{cases}
\]

---

## (a) CDF of \(T\)

For \(0\le t\le 1\),

\[
\{T\le t\}
=
\left\{X\le t,\ \frac{X+Y}{2}\le t\right\}
=
\{X\le t,\ X+Y\le 2t\}.
\]

Thus

\[
F_T(t)=\int_0^t \min\{1,2t-x\}\,dx.
\]

If \(0\le t\le 1/2\), then \(2t-x\le 1\), so

\[
F_T(t)=\int_0^t (2t-x)\,dx
=2t^2-\frac{t^2}{2}
=\frac32 t^2.
\]

If \(1/2\le t\le 1\), then \(2t-x\ge 1\) for \(0\le x\le 2t-1\). Therefore

\[
F_T(t)=\int_0^{2t-1}1\,dx+\int_{2t-1}^t(2t-x)\,dx.
\]

The second integral is

\[
\int_{2t-1}^t(2t-x)\,dx
=\frac{1-t^2}{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
F_T(t)=2t-1+\frac{1-t^2}{2}
=2t-\frac12-\frac{t^2}{2}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
F_T(t)=
\begin{cases}
0, & t<0,\\[4pt]
\dfrac32 t^2, & 0\le t\le \dfrac12,\\[8pt]
2t-\dfrac12-\dfrac{t^2}{2}, & \dfrac12\le t\le 1,\\[8pt]
1, & t\ge 1.
\end{cases}}
\]

The density is therefore

\[
f_T(t)=
\begin{cases}
3t, & 0<t<1/2,\\[4pt]
2-t, & 1/2<t<1.
\end{cases}
\]

---

## (b) \(\mathbb E[T]\)

Using \(\mathbb E[T]=\int_0^1 \mathbb P(T>t)\,dt\),

\[
\mathbb E[T]
=
\int_0^{1/2}\left(1-\frac32 t^2\right)\,dt
+
\int_{1/2}^1\left(1-2t+\frac12+\frac{t^2}{2}\right)\,dt.
\]

The first integral is

\[
\int_0^{1/2}\left(1-\frac32 t^2\right)\,dt
=
\left[t-\frac12 t^3\right]_0^{1/2}
=
\frac12-\frac1{16}
=
\frac7{16}.
\]

The second integral is

\[
\int_{1/2}^1\left(\frac32-2t+\frac{t^2}{2}\right)\,dt
=
\left[\frac32 t-t^2+\frac{t^3}{6}\right]_{1/2}^1
=
\frac7{48}.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{\mathbb E[T]=\frac7{16}+\frac7{48}=\frac7{12}.}
\]

---

## (c) \(\mathbb E[X_1\mid T=t]\)

We derive the conditional law of \(X=X_1\) given \(T=t\).

For Borel sets \(B,C\subseteq [0,1]\),

\[
\mathbb P(X\in B,T\in C)
=
\int_B \left[x\mathbf 1_C(x)+2\int_x^{(x+1)/2}\mathbf 1_C(t)\,dt\right]dx.
\]

Switching the order of integration, let

\[
a(t)=\max\{0,2t-1\}.
\]

Then

\[
\mathbb P(X\in B,T\in C)
=
\int_C \left[t\mathbf 1_B(t)+2\int_{a(t)}^t \mathbf 1_B(x)\,dx\right]dt.
\]

Thus a regular conditional distribution of \(X_1\) given \(T=t\) is

\[
\mathbb P(X_1\in dx\mid T=t)
=
\frac{t\,\delta_t(dx)+2\mathbf 1_{[a(t),t]}(x)\,dx}{t+2(t-a(t))}.
\]

Therefore, for bounded measurable \(g\),

\[
\mathbb E[g(X_1)\mid T=t]
=
\frac{t g(t)+2\int_{a(t)}^t g(x)\,dx}{t+2(t-a(t))}.
\]

Taking \(g(x)=x\),

\[
\mathbb E[X_1\mid T=t]
=
\frac{t^2+2\int_{a(t)}^t x\,dx}{t+2(t-a(t))}
=
\frac{2t^2-a(t)^2}{3t-2a(t)}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E[X_1\mid T=t]
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2t}{3}, & 0\le t\le \dfrac12,\\[10pt]
\dfrac{-2t^2+4t-1}{2-t}, & \dfrac12\le t\le 1.
\end{cases}}
\]

At \(t=1/2\), both formulas give \(1/3\).

---

## (d) \(\operatorname{Var}(X_1\mid T=t)\)

Using the same conditional distribution,

\[
\mathbb E[X_1^2\mid T=t]
=
\frac{t^3+2\int_{a(t)}^t x^2\,dx}{t+2(t-a(t))}
=
\frac{t^3+\frac23(t^3-a(t)^3)}{3t-2a(t)}.
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbb E[X_1^2\mid T=t]
=
\frac{\frac53 t^3-\frac23 a(t)^3}{3t-2a(t)}.
\]

### Case 1: \(0\le t\le 1/2\)

Then \(a(t)=0\), so

\[
\mathbb E[X_1^2\mid T=t]
=
\frac{\frac53 t^3}{3t}
=
\frac59 t^2.
\]

Since

\[
\mathbb E[X_1\mid T=t]=\frac{2t}{3},
\]

we get

\[
\operatorname{Var}(X_1\mid T=t)
=
\frac59 t^2-\frac49 t^2
=
\frac19 t^2.
\]

### Case 2: \(1/2\le t\le 1\)

Then \(a(t)=2t-1\). After simplification,

\[
\operatorname{Var}(X_1\mid T=t)
=
\frac{(1-t)^3(1+t)}{3(2-t)^2}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Var}(X_1\mid T=t)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{t^2}{9}, & 0\le t\le \dfrac12,\\[10pt]
\dfrac{(1-t)^3(1+t)}{3(2-t)^2}, & \dfrac12\le t\le 1.
\end{cases}}
\]

At \(t=1/2\), both formulas give \(1/36\), and at \(t=1\) the conditional variance is \(0\).
